blocks.task_summary: Use S₄ = 40 and S₅ = 65 to find p and q where Sₙ = pn² − qn, by forming two equations from the given sum formula and solving the simultaneous linear system for p and q.
method_path: Substitute n=4, S₄=40 into Sₙ=pn²−qn to obtain 16p−4q=40 → 4p−q=10
Substitute n=5, S₅=65 into Sₙ=pn²−qn to obtain 25p−5q=65 → 5p−q=13
Solve the simultaneous linear equations, e.g., subtract to get p=3, then back-substitute to get q=2
accepted_alternatives: Use arithmetic sequence sum formula Sₙ = n/2(2u₁+(n−1)d) to form equations in u₁ and d, solve to get u₁=1 and d=6, then equate coefficients in Sₙ = 3n²−2n to obtain p=3, q=2.

evidence.basis: METHOD 1: attempt to form at least one equation using S₄ or S₅ (M1); 25p−5q=65 → 5p−q=13 and 40=16p−4q → 10=4p−q (A1); valid attempt to solve simultaneous linear equations in p and q (M1); p=3, q=2 (A1A1). METHOD 2: attempt to form equation using S₄ or S₅ (M1); gives equations in u₁ and d (A1); solve to get u₁=1, d=6 (A1); equate to Sₙ = 3n²−2n giving p=3, q=2 (A1).

blocks.task_summary: Find the fifth term u₅ of the arithmetic sequence using u₅ = S₅ − S₄ = 65 − 40 = 25.
accepted_alternatives: Use u₅ = u₁ + 4d with u₁=1, d=6 giving u₅ = 1 + 4×6 = 25.
Use S₅ = 5(u₁ + u₅)/2 = 65 with u₁=1 to solve for u₅ = 25.

evidence.basis: u₅ = S₅ − S₄ OR substituting u₁ and d into u₅ = u₁ + 4d OR substituting u₁ into S₅ = 5(u₁+u₅)/2 = 65 (M1); u₅ = 65 − 40 = 25 (A1).
